summary: Describes conventions for using cryptographic algorithms with the Cryptographic Message Syntax to protect the symmetric key package content type, covering SignedData, EnvelopedData, EncryptedData and AuthEnvelopedData. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC lists which existing cryptographic algorithms implementations must or should support when CMS protects symmetric key packages. It covers signing, encryption, authenticated encryption, and public-key sizes.

subtitle: Algorithm support requirements for CMS protection of symmetric key packages.

tldr.problem: Implementers need interoperable algorithm requirements when CMS protects a symmetric key package.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC sets MUST, SHOULD, and MAY algorithm requirements for SignedData, EnvelopedData, EncryptedData, and AuthEnvelopedData.
tldr.outcome: It defines no new algorithms and specifies a common baseline using existing algorithms.

today: RFC 6160 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Scope of the Algorithm Rules
sections.content:
The RFC describes conventions for using cryptographic algorithms with Cryptographic Message Syntax to protect the symmetric key package content type. It covers SignedData, EnvelopedData, EncryptedData, and AuthEnvelopedData.

It does not define new algorithms; it refers to algorithms specified elsewhere.
sections.plainLanguage: The document gives implementation rules for existing algorithms in four CMS content types. It does not create a new algorithm.

sections.title: Signed and Enveloped Data
sections.content:
For SignedData, implementations MUST support RSA and SHA-256, and SHOULD support RSASSA-PSS, DSA, and SHA-1. ECDSA MAY be supported. For EnvelopedData, key transport MUST be implemented; RSA encryption MUST be supported and RSAES-OAEP SHOULD be supported.

If key agreement is used, ephemeral-static Diffie-Hellman MUST be supported and ECDH MAY be supported. AES-128 Key Wrap with Padding MUST be supported, and AES-256 SHOULD be supported.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC separates required, recommended, and optional algorithms. Implementations use the required set to improve interoperability.

sections.title: Other Content Types and Key Sizes
sections.content:
EncryptedData MUST implement AES-128 Key Wrap with Padding and SHOULD implement AES-256. AuthEnvelopedData follows EnvelopedData's rules, but MUST use AES-GCM for content encryption: 128-bit AES-GCM MUST be implemented and 256-bit SHOULD be implemented. AES-CCM MAY also be supported.

Implementations supporting the listed RSA, DSA, or Diffie-Hellman algorithms MUST support key lengths from 1024-bit to 2048-bit inclusive. ECDSA and ECDH implementations MUST support P-256.
sections.plainLanguage: Each CMS content type has required algorithms and key sizes. AuthEnvelopedData must support the 128-bit AES-GCM version.
